sections.heading: Why a School Zone Speeding Ticket Is Worse Than a Normal One
paragraphs: Texas treats speeding in an active school zone as the same Class C misdemeanor as any other speeding ticket, but courts don't treat it the same. Judges in El Paso County tend to set school zone fines at the top of the range, court costs are added, and the citation carries a stigma that shows up in how the prosecutor approaches your case.

The bigger problem is the driving safety course. Under Code of Criminal Procedure art. 45A.352 (formerly art. 45.0511), a driver can normally dismiss a speeding ticket by completing a six-hour defensive driving course. Courts may refuse it in certain cases, and school zone speeding is one of the most common refusals in El Paso. CDL holders are excluded by statute regardless of the court, and anyone who used the course in the last 12 months is out too.

That leaves a conviction on your DPS record, visible to your insurer at renewal, unless someone negotiates something better. This page is general information, not legal advice about your case, but it is the clearest example of a ticket you should not just pay.

sections.heading: El Paso School Zones Where These Tickets Are Written
paragraphs: El Paso's three big districts — EPISD, YISD and SISD — have campuses sitting directly on arterial roads, which is where school zone enforcement concentrates. On the East Side, schools front Montana Avenue, Zaragoza Road, Pebble Hills and George Dieter, where the regular limit of 40 or 45 mph drops to 20 or 25 when the lights flash. The same pattern holds along Mesa Street, Resler Drive and Redd Road on the West Side, North Loop and Alameda in the Lower Valley, and Dyer Street in the Northeast.

Officers know the drop-off and pickup windows and set up in the zone with radar or lidar for the full period. The drivers they stop are mostly commuters who travel that road every day and didn't register the lights, or who were already slowing but hadn't reached 20 yet when the reading was taken.

Where the ticket is filed depends on the officer. El Paso Police tickets go to El Paso Municipal Court. Horizon City, Socorro, San Elizario, Clint and Anthony enforce their own zones and hear them in their municipal courts, while a Sheriff's deputy or DPS trooper ticket goes to a Justice of the Peace precinct.

sections.heading: The Flashing-Light Timing Defense
paragraphs: A school zone limit only applies when the zone is active. In most El Paso zones that means the yellow beacons are flashing; some rely on posted hours instead. If the lights weren't on when you passed the sign, there was no school zone offense — at most an ordinary speeding ticket, with the usual access to deferred disposition and defensive driving.

Timing disputes are common at the edges of the window. The beacons run on a schedule that doesn't necessarily match actual bell times, early-release days or district calendars. We ask every client for the exact time on the citation, compare it to the posted hours and the district's calendar, and when there's a gap we put it in front of the prosecutor.

list.text: If not, the school zone limit was not in effect. The time on the citation versus the posted hours is the first thing we check.
Holidays, teacher work days and early-release days are frequent sources of timer errors.
A speed clocked before you reached the zone sign is not a school zone speed.
Radar and lidar need calibration records, and a missing log is leverage in negotiation.

sections.heading: When Defensive Driving Is Off the Table, Here Is What We Ask For
paragraphs: When you hire us online or call 915-503-1600, we file a notice of appearance promptly so the appearance date can't turn into a failure-to-appear warrant. We pull the citation and officer notes, check the calibration records, build the timing questions above, and take the case to the pretrial docket.

Because defensive driving is often unavailable, the goal is usually a deferred disposition: a court fee, a clean deferral period, and a dismissal with no conviction. Where the timing or the reading is genuinely weak, we push for an outright dismissal. When neither is available, we ask for an amended, non-moving charge so the words "school zone" do not reach your DPS record. You generally do not need to appear. Se habla español.

sections.heading: CDL Drivers, Enhanced-Fine Signs and Insurance
paragraphs: If you hold a commercial license, a school zone ticket in your personal car still counts. CDL holders cannot use the defensive driving dismissal, and employers who pull your record will see a school zone conviction as exactly what it looks like. Deferred disposition is likewise unavailable to a commercial driver's license holder for a motor vehicle control violation (Code Crim. Proc. art. 45A.301), so a dismissal or an amended charge is what we work toward in those cases.

You may also see "fines doubled" signage in some zones; Texas allows enhanced fines in certain designated areas, and the court sets the amount. Add court costs, and a school zone ticket paid outright can run several hundred dollars before any insurance effect begins. A conviction may affect premiums depending on your history and carrier, and Texas no longer uses the former Driver Responsibility Program points system — but repeated moving-violation convictions can still affect your record and may lead to suspension in some circumstances. Against that, a flat $59 or $69 attorney fee is a modest cost.

sections.heading: Evidence to Gather This Week, and What to Send the Office
paragraphs: Note the exact time on the citation and, if you can, drive back through the zone at that time on a school day and photograph the beacon and the posted hours. Write down whether the lights were flashing when you passed, whether you had already begun slowing, and where the officer was sitting.

Then protect the appearance date. Don't pay the ticket, don't request defensive driving yourself — in a school zone case that request can be denied after you've entered a plea — and don't miss the date. If it already passed, use the free ticket and warrant lookup or read our warrant recall page and call us today.

faqs.q: Can I take defensive driving for a school zone speeding ticket in El Paso?
faqs.a: Often not. Courts may refuse the driving safety course in certain cases, and school zone speeding is one of the most common refusals in El Paso County. CDL holders are excluded by statute. That is why we usually negotiate for deferred disposition or an amended charge instead.

faqs.q: How much is a school zone speeding ticket in El Paso?
faqs.a: The fine is set by the judge, and school zone cases are often set at the high end of the range, with court costs added. Paid outright, the total can run several hundred dollars, and a conviction may also affect your insurance depending on your carrier and record.

faqs.q: The lights weren't flashing when I drove through. Does that matter?
faqs.a: It can be the whole case. The reduced limit applies only when the zone is active, which in most El Paso zones means the beacons are on. We compare the citation time with the posted hours and the school calendar, and when they don't line up we raise it with the prosecutor.

faqs.q: I was slowing down but hadn't reached 20 yet. Is that a defense?
faqs.a: It's a real issue. Where the officer took the reading relative to the zone sign matters, and so does whether your speed was still dropping. Those facts go into negotiation for deferred disposition even when the court won't offer defensive driving.

faqs.q: I have a CDL. What happens with a school zone ticket?
faqs.a: You can't use the driving safety course, and deferred disposition is generally unavailable to CDL holders, so the goal is a dismissal or an amended charge that keeps the conviction off your record.

faqs.q: Do I have to appear in court?
faqs.a: Generally not for a school zone ticket in El Paso County. We file the appearance, negotiate at the pretrial docket and report the result. A trial is uncommon, and we would talk it through with you first.
